headline: Gujarat HC: Service tax paid after DGGI inquiry refundable under Sec 142(3) CGST Act
reference: M/s Filatex India Limited vs Commissioner of Central Excise and Service Tax, Vadodara-II, R/Tax Appeal No. 883 of 2024, Gujarat High Court (Neutral Citation: GJHC240561622024)
summary_points: Issue: whether service tax of ₹36,34,040 paid on ECB services after a DGGI inquiry was 'recovery' under Section 142(8)(a) CGST Act, barring refund.
Held: Section 142(8)(a) applies only where assessment or adjudication proceedings were instituted; none existed here, so payment was voluntary.
CESTAT and Commissioner (Appeals) orders were quashed; refund claim to be processed under Section 142(3) read with Section 174(2)(c).
Matter remanded to the Adjudicating Authority; the appellant gave up its claim to interest on the refund.
Impact: pre-GST dues paid after inquiry, without formal assessment or adjudication, may still support a Cenvat refund claim.
who_is_affected: Taxpayers who paid pre-GST service tax or excise dues after DGGI/departmental inquiry, without any assessment or adjudication, and could not take Cenvat credit after 1 July 2017.
action_required: Review similar pending or rejected refund claims under Section 142(3) CGST Act and check whether any assessment or adjudication proceedings had actually been initiated.

social.linkedin:
Gujarat High Court on Section 142(8)(a) CGST Act: payment after an inquiry is not 'recovery' without assessment or adjudication.

In M/s Filatex India Limited vs Commissioner of Central Excise and Service Tax, Vadodara-II, the appellant paid ₹36,34,040 of service tax (with interest and penalty) on external commercial borrowing services under reverse charge after a DGGI inquiry. Its refund claim was rejected by the adjudicating authority, the Commissioner (Appeals) and CESTAT.

The High Court held that Section 142(8)(a) applies only where assessment or adjudication proceedings were instituted. None had been initiated here, so the payment was treated as voluntary.

The Court quashed the lower orders and remanded the matter to process the refund under Section 142(3) read with Section 174 of the CGST Act. The appellant gave up its claim to interest.

For taxpayers with pre-GST dues paid after inquiry, this ruling may open a path to refund where no formal proceedings were initiated.

Please verify with the official judgment before relying on it.
